spec: docs/GROUP_CALLS_V2_SPEC.md sections 5.1-5.4; P12 frame anti-replay (WIRE_SPEC section 11)
description: Frame-crypto vectors (group calls v2 and 1:1): native FrameCryptor wire, AES-256-GCM, aes_key = HKDF-SHA256(ikm=K[M,E], salt=empty, info=128x0x00, L=32), keyIndex = epoch mod 16. Two senders, epochs 1..17 (index wraps 16 -> 0, 17 -> 1). v2: the IV counter is a full uint32 (cases[] all use counter 0 and are byte-identical to v1), plus counterCases[] and replayScenarios[] for the receiver anti-replay window. Generated by scripts/group-e2ee-kat-dump.mjs using node:crypto only.
wireLayout: header(unencryptedBytes) || ciphertext || tag(16) || iv(12) || [12, keyIndex]; AAD = header; H.264/H.265: the tail ciphertext || tag || iv || trailer is RBSP-escaped on the wire and MUST be unescaped before the trailer and the IV are read
ivLayout: ssrc(4 BE) || rtpTimestamp(4 BE) || ((rtpTimestamp - counter) mod 2^32)(4 BE), counter = full uint32 per ssrc (cases[]: counter 0, the first frame of the ssrc)

replayRules.identity: participant handler, ivSsrc = IV word 1, counter = (IV word 2 - IV word 3) mod 2^32
replayRules.order: key lookup (missing_key) -> reflection/duplicate/too_old pre-check -> AEAD (decrypt_failed) -> commit (cap)
replayRules.casesNote: Every cases[] frame and every ringScenarios[] frame has counter 0 on the same ssrc, and ringScenarios re-open frames across steps: a consumer MUST use a fresh replay window (or clear it) before each open of those two sections. Only replayScenarios[] exercise the window.
replayRules.scenarioSteps: install: set the participant key slots (an identical key is a no-op, a different key at an occupied slot garbage-collects windows); deliver: open the pool frame replayFrames[id] and compare the verdict with expect

ringScenarios.name: wrap-overwrites-slot
ringScenarios.description: Epochs 1..16 installed for sender A fill slots 1..15,0; installing epoch 17 overwrites slot 1 (17 % 16 = 1): the epoch-1 key is gone, epoch-2..16 keys still open.

ringScenarios.name: missing-key
ringScenarios.description: A frame whose keyIndex slot has no key yet must be dropped as missing_key (receiver then sends media_key_nack).

ringScenarios.name: per-participant-isolation
ringScenarios.description: Rings are per participant: sender A's key at slot 5 never opens sender B's epoch-5 frame (same index, other key): decrypt_failed, not missing_key.

replayScenarios.name: in-order
replayScenarios.description: Frames 0..5 of one stream in order: every one is accepted once.

replayScenarios.name: duplicate
replayScenarios.description: A frame delivered twice (same mid, another mid, or a re-created cryptor: the window lives in the participant handler) is a duplicate, whatever the delivery order.

replayScenarios.name: reorder-255-ok-256-too-old
replayScenarios.description: top = 256: counter 1 is 255 behind (inside the 256-frame window and never seen: ok), counter 0 is 256 behind (too_old); an accepted late frame is then a duplicate.

replayScenarios.name: jump-255-keeps-bit
replayScenarios.description: A forward jump of exactly 255 keeps the old top as bit 255: counter 0 is a duplicate, not too_old.

replayScenarios.name: jump-over-window
replayScenarios.description: A forward jump of >= 256 resets the bitmap to 1: everything older than the new top - 255 is too_old, the frame just below the new top is still accepted once.

replayScenarios.name: simulcast-two-ssrcs
replayScenarios.description: Two ssrcs of one participant (simulcast layers) have independent windows: the same counter on the other ssrc is fresh; switching back to a layer after a jump is accepted.

replayScenarios.name: key-switch-late-old-slot
replayScenarios.description: The counter keeps increasing across a key switch and the window is shared across slots: a late epoch-1 frame inside the window is accepted once, then it is a duplicate.

replayScenarios.name: slot-overwrite-gc
replayScenarios.description: Re-installing the IDENTICAL key at a slot is a no-op (the window must not reset). Installing a DIFFERENT key at an occupied slot (epoch 17 over epoch 1, slot 1) clears that slot from every window and erases the windows left with no slot: an old epoch-1 frame is decrypt_failed, a fresh-key frame opens a new window (even counter 0, whose old window is gone).

replayScenarios.name: slot-overwrite-gc-fresh-window
replayScenarios.description: The window of a stream whose only key was overwritten is erased: the same counter under the fresh key is accepted again (a new window), proving the garbage collection.

replayScenarios.name: reflection
replayScenarios.description: A frame whose ssrc is a LOCAL send ssrc of the same handler (1:1: our own frame reflected back) is rejected before anything else; other ssrcs are unaffected.

replayScenarios.name: failed-aead-never-commits
replayScenarios.description: Only an authenticated frame touches the window: a tampered ciphertext and a forged high counter (IV word 3 rewritten) are decrypt_failed and leave the window as it was, so the genuine frames still open once.

replayScenarios.name: missing-key-never-commits
replayScenarios.description: A frame for an empty slot is missing_key and consumes nothing; after the key arrives the same frame opens once.

replayScenarios.name: cap-65th-stream
replayScenarios.description: At most 64 streams (ssrcs) per participant: the 65th new authenticated stream is rejected with cap (fail-closed, never evicts) while the existing windows keep working.
